catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extracted from Continuous Architecture Steering (CAS) runner, governance engine, and multi-agent steering infrastructure.
analysis_limits: Repository source code and directory hierarchy
No dynamic execution traces or live external LLM call inspection

system_map.overview: Continuous Architecture Steering (CAS) system that guides, evaluates, and merges software architecture artifacts generated by AI agents and humans using deterministic governance rules and LLM evaluation steps.

agents.name: AgenticMerger
agents.role: Resolves governance conflicts and merges architecture knowledge blocks across repositories and branches.

agents.name: ComplianceEngine
agents.role: Evaluates architectural deltas against governance constraints, generating compliance metrics and findings.

agents.name: GovernanceActionEngine
agents.role: Executes state transitions and policy enforcement actions guided by a transition registry.

agents.name: FlowRunner
agents.role: Orchestrates multi-step continuous architecture steering, facts generation, and evaluation workflows.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner manages pipeline execution stages, sequentially driving git delta detection, compliance verification, and agentic merge resolution.

tools_and_integrations.name: LiteLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Provides unified access to multi-provider foundation models with fallback handling.

tools_and_integrations.name: MockLLMClient
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Enables deterministic offline evaluation and testing of governance flows without external API calls.

tools_and_integrations.name: Git Delta Extractor
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Parses repository diffs into structured delta models for agent steering.

tools_and_integrations.name: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
tools_and_integrations.purpose: Captures traces and latency metrics for agent decision lifecycles.

state_and_memory.description: Version-controlled architectural decisions, rules, models, and capabilities stored as YAML/JSON/Markdown in cas-knowledge.
Runtime indices, capabilities lineage, and prompt facts projected from repository state.
Compliance findings, metrics, and transition action states passed through pipeline context.

patterns.name: Steering Projection Context Injection

tool_protocols.notes: Injects structured markdown and JSON steering directives into agent config files.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures that autonomous coding agents adhere to global governance rules by projecting them directly into their instructions.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Leaves reasoning to the agent while strictly constraining boundary conditions via embedded instruction blocks.

patterns.summary: Injects centrally managed governance rules, capability bounds, and architectural constraints directly into agent entry points.
patterns.intent: Constrain autonomous agent decision-making within architectural and operational guardrails by synchronizing knowledge blocks into instruction files.
patterns.context: Used during workspace bootstrapping and synchronization workflows (e.g., AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md).
forces: Agents lose architectural alignment when context windows omit enterprise guidelines.
Manually copying rules to every agent profile creates drift.
patterns.solution: Generate deterministic governance blocks from cas-knowledge and merge them into agent configuration files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) using automated marker delimitation.
implementation_signals: Markers like <!-- CAS:START --> and <!-- CAS:END --> in instruction files
Bootstrap scripts updating AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md dynamically

evidence.note: Merges authoritative CAS governance blocks into target agent markdown documents.
Automated workflow synchronizing managed steering projections across workspace files.

benefits: Consistent architectural constraints across varied agent vendors (Claude, Gemini, agents-cli).
Auditability of agent prompt contexts through Git version control.
costs: Requires synchronization workflows whenever governance policies update.
failure_modes: Accidental removal or modification of CAS delimiting tags by developers causing merge failures.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adaptable to any agent runtime that ingests markdown-based project manuals or instructions.

patterns.name: Schema-Enforced Governance Action Engine

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions are governed by typed registry and Pydantic validation.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unauthorized state transitions and unparseable agent modifications.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Rigid state machine boundaries prevent autonomous execution drifts.

patterns.summary: Restricts agent and system lifecycle changes to pre-registered state transitions validated against strongly-typed schemas.
patterns.intent: Prevent invalid status progressions or unauthorized mutations during automated architecture modifications.
patterns.context: Governing architectural decisions, exceptions, and promotions in cas-knowledge.
forces: Unchecked agent actions can corrupt lifecycle metadata or bypass review stages.
Free-text LLM evaluations lack deterministic guarantees.
patterns.solution: Define allowable states in a TransitionRegistry and require all GovernanceActions to pass schema validation before triggering side effects.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class checking source and target states
Pydantic models defining GovernanceAction and ComplianceFinding

evidence.note: Enforces state transition rules and executes validated governance actions.
Typed models defining structural constraints for all governance operations.

benefits: Clear audit log of compliant and non-compliant operations.
costs: Changes to lifecycle states require updating the registry code and schemas.
failure_modes: Rigid transition definitions blocking valid edge-case remediations.

patterns.reuse_notes: Extractable as a reusable governance enforcement layer over agentic workflows.

patterns.name: Pluggable LLM Gateway with Mock Fallback

tool_protocols.notes: Wraps multi-provider LLM calling via litellm with offline mock substitution.

optimisation_targets.notes: Ensures full CI validation without external API dependency or token expenditure.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Decouples business logic from specific proprietary LLM APIs.

patterns.summary: Abstracts LLM invocation behind a unified client protocol that allows seamless swapping between production model routing and local deterministic mocks.
patterns.intent: Allow agent flows to run seamlessly in cost-free CI environments and local unit tests while retaining multi-provider flexibility in production.
patterns.context: LLM client integration used across runner evaluation flows and agentic merging.
forces: CI pipelines cannot reliably or affordably depend on external LLM APIs with fluctuating rate limits and tokens.
Code tightly coupled to specific LLM SDKs resists model migrations.
patterns.solution: Expose a shared LLM client interface implemented by LiteLLMClient for live deployments and MockLLMClient for deterministic fixture-based testing.

evidence.note: Wraps multi-provider LLM calls via litellm.
Provides fixture-driven deterministic mock responses for agent operations.

benefits: Provider-agnostic prompt execution (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock).
costs: Mocks must be kept aligned with real LLM response shapes.
failure_modes: Mocks drift from real LLM failure cases (e.g. malformed JSON outputs in production).

patterns.reuse_notes: Standard pattern for testable agentic infrastructure.

patterns.name: Agentic Semantic Merge Reconciliation

tool_protocols.notes: Synthesizes Git deltas and text conflicts into merged architectural documents.

optimisation_targets.notes: Automates non-trivial merging of divergent architecture specifications.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Delegates semantic understanding of multi-party architectural updates to an LLM.

patterns.summary: Employs an agentic resolver to reconcile semantic conflicts across distributed architectural documentation and governance blocks.
patterns.intent: Resolve complex textual and structural conflicts in architecture artifacts that standard 3-way git merges fail to handle gracefully.
patterns.context: Reconciling conflicting decisions and governance updates across feature branches.
forces: Git merges create text collision markers that break YAML/Markdown parsing.
Architecture updates contain semantic nuance requiring domain context to merge accurately.
patterns.solution: Feed base, left, and right branches along with raw git deltas into AgenticMerger, which leverages an LLM to generate a synthesized ResolutionResult.
implementation_signals: ResolutionResult model tracking resolved outputs and confidence metrics

evidence.note: Reconciles conflicting document versions using LLM reasoning.
Captures the structured outcome of an agentic merge operation.

benefits: Preserves document integrity and YAML validity across branch merges.
Reduces developer toil in reconciling architectural documentation.
costs: Risk of silent semantic hallucination or unintended omission of critical rules.
Requires human review for low-confidence resolutions.
failure_modes: Hallucinating resolved text that alters governance constraints without triggering schema errors.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to any GitOps documentation or specification repository.

patterns.name: Git Delta Capability Lineage Derivation

tool_protocols.notes: Extracts capability mutations from commit histories and diffs.

optimisation_targets.notes: Grounds architectural knowledge in concrete Git commits rather than unverified agent memory.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Relies on immutable Git history as the sole source of truth.

patterns.summary: Derives agent capabilities and architectural evolution directly from immutable Git change deltas rather than transient conversational state.
patterns.intent: Ground architectural state transitions and agent context in verifiable repository changes.
patterns.context: Tracking system evolution across commits to generate steering runtime indices and capability sets.
forces: Agent summaries suffer from drift and hallucination over time.
Manual tracking of system capabilities is seldom maintained by developers.
patterns.solution: Model raw Git changes as typed RawGitDelta objects, mapping modifications to CapabilityRecords and CapabilityLineage.
implementation_signals: RawGitDelta, CapabilitySet, CapabilityLineage, and ArchitecturalDelta models in steering/models.py

evidence.note: Defines typed structures tracking capability evolution mapped to Git commits.

benefits: Audit trail directly linked to cryptographic commit hashes.
Prevents memory corruption or loss across agent session resets.
costs: Parsing large or noisy diffs can result in high token overhead.
Requires strict commit discipline or branch hygiene.
failure_modes: Squash or rebase operations destroying lineage relationships if commit hashes change.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any CI/CD or agentic system operating on Git repositories.

patterns.name: Sequential Pipeline Orchestration with Context Propagation

tool_protocols.notes: Steps pass typed execution context linearly.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees evaluation occurs prior to promotion or merge execution.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Sequential execution ensures predictable lifecycle step ordering.

patterns.summary: Executes governance, evaluation, and merge operations in a controlled multi-stage sequence passing strongly-typed state context across steps.
patterns.intent: Coordinate multi-stage architectural evaluation and sync operations with explicit sequencing and rollback capability.
patterns.context: Executing CAS CLI runs, projection building, and automated compliance checks.
forces: Ad-hoc step invocation leads to unvalidated changes entering production branches.
Monolithic scripts obscure where execution failures happen.
patterns.solution: FlowRunner coordinates pipeline stages, ensuring each stage accepts validated input models and produces typed outputs for downstream consumers.
implementation_signals: CLI command dispatch passing context to runner

evidence.note: Implements the central execution runner coordinating steering tasks.

benefits: Clear failure boundaries and step isolation.
Deterministic execution flow enabling reproducible audits.
costs: Limits concurrent step execution when steps are strictly linear.
failure_modes: Pipeline halts completely if an early optional step raises an unhandled exception.

patterns.reuse_notes: Foundation for building CLI-driven agent workflow orchestrators.

patterns.name: Declarative Template-Governed Knowledge Artifacts

tool_protocols.notes: Agents parse and generate markdown files structured around fixed frontmatter and section headings.

optimisation_targets.notes: Constrains LLM output structure to standardized architectural documentation schemas.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Guides LLM generation into structured sections without requiring brittle JSON-only generation for human-facing docs.

patterns.summary: Enforces strict document schematization across human and agent outputs using standardized markdown templates and frontmatter.
patterns.intent: Maintain uniform structure and semantic parseability across diverse architectural artifacts (ADRs, patterns, signals, decisions) created by LLMs and humans.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge template definitions used to prompt and validate agent outputs.
forces: LLMs produce inconsistent documentation layouts when given open-ended instructions.
Static JSON schemas fail to support rich prose and architectural diagram embeddings.
patterns.solution: Define declarative markdown templates with explicit metadata headers and section prompts for patterns, decisions, and heuristics.

evidence.note: Standardized ADR layout for agent generation.
Canonical pattern schema including forces, context, and consequences.
Formal schema for promoting heuristics to established patterns.

benefits: Enables downstream programmatic parsing and validation via regex or frontmatter parsers.
costs: Formatting drift occurs if agents truncate markdown sections or fail to populate template fields.
failure_modes: Malformed YAML frontmatter breaking static site generators (MkDocs).

patterns.reuse_notes: Easily ported to any documentation-driven development or architecture governance repository.

patterns.name: Multi-Metric Governance Health Evaluator

tool_protocols.notes: Derives aggregated categorical status (Healthy, Warning, Critical) from metrics.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents downstream publication or deployment if critical compliance thresholds are breached.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Deterministic threshold math is preferred over non-deterministic LLM score judgments.

patterns.summary: Computes composite governance health and risk categorizations using transparent mathematical heuristics over compliance metrics.
patterns.intent: Transform raw compliance findings into actionable categorical health evaluations to gate CI/CD and agent workflows.
patterns.context: Dashboard calculation and PR gating checks.
forces: Raw metric counts overwhelm human reviewers and downstream CI bots.
Subjective agent ratings of 'health' lack reproducibility.
patterns.solution: Execute calculate_health to aggregate compliance finding counts, risk severities, and unresolved exceptions into a HealthStatus with explanatory reason strings.
implementation_signals: calculate_health and get_health_reasons functions in dashboard/health_model.py

evidence.note: Evaluates compliance health status and computes diagnostic failure explanations.
Models holding aggregated risk metrics and status records.

benefits: Objective, auditable pass/fail criteria for PR checks.
Clear diagnostic reasons pinpointing exact rule violations.
costs: Fixed threshold logic can trigger false alarms during large migrations.
failure_modes: Misconfigured threshold causing continuous pipeline failure under acceptable technical debt.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be integrated into any agentic CI gatekeeper to block unsafe merges.

anti_patterns.name: Unbounded Unvalidated Governance Mutation
symptoms: Autonomous agents editing cas-knowledge rules or templates without running TransitionRegistry checks.
Commit messages indicating direct governance alterations bypassing FlowRunner.

where_observed.note: Merger relies on LLM synthesis that could modify rule constraints if prompt lacks schema enforcement.

impact: Governance rules weaken over time as agents optimize away constraints to resolve merge conflicts quickly.
Undetected security or architectural regressions across repositories.
suggested_remediation: Enforce pre-commit or CI hooks that validate all governance rule changes against ComplianceEngine before committing.
Require cryptographic or human approval signatures for transitions in cas-knowledge/global/rules/.

anti_patterns.name: Mock-Production Prompt Contract Divergence
symptoms: Tests pass completely green with MockLLMClient, but live runs fail with unparseable JSON or schema validation exceptions.
Mock client returns idealized outputs that ignore token limits, model refusals, or malformed syntax.

where_observed.note: Static responses do not simulate LLM hallucinations or schema failures.

impact: False sense of security in CI pipelines.
Runtime crashes when calling production models via LiteLLMClient.
suggested_remediation: Implement schema fuzzing or synthetic corruption in MockLLMClient to test agent error-handling loops.
Maintain periodic integration runs against live LLM endpoints using recorded and replayed network responses.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: System-level rules and steering context are embedded as markdown sections delimited by fixed HTML comment tags (<!-- CAS:START --> / <!-- CAS:END -->), complemented by structured Pydantic models for inputs and outputs.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Guarantees predictable boundaries between human instructions and automated steering context.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Multi-tier evaluation combining static compliance analysis, state transition verification via registry, and deterministic health status calculations.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Avoids relying solely on LLMs to evaluate LLM-generated changes.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Traceable metrics and OpenTelemetry instrumentation integrated into runtime execution models.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Enables distributed tracing across agent steering operations and pipeline steps.

open_questions.question: How are unresolvable semantic merge conflicts escalated to humans during automated GitHub Actions runs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: If AgenticMerger fails or yields a low confidence score, the pipeline must either block the PR or fall back to standard Git conflict markers.
open_questions.evidence_gap: The exact threshold and notification mechanism for human-in-the-loop escalation in cas-continuous-architecture.yml was not fully visible.

open_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether CAS supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) or standard CLI subshell tool calling for skill execution.
open_questions.evidence_gap: Skills directory exists (.agents/skills/hf-cli/) but adapter code was not in the core runner manifest.
